question: Constriction of the afferent aeriole to the kidney glomerulus results in:

options.opa: Reduction of glomerular filtration rate and decreased urinary output
options.opc: Increased glomerular filtration rate and no change in urine output.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Constriction of afferent arteriole -> Decreased blood flow to glomerulus -> Reduced hydrostatic pressure in glomerulus -> Decreased glomerular filtration rate -> Reduction of urinary output -> 95%
CHAIN: Constriction of afferent arteriole -> Decreased blood flow to glomerulus -> Reduced glomerular filtration rate -> Decreased urinary output -> 90%
CHAIN: Constriction of afferent arteriole -> Decreased perfusion pressure in glomerulus -> Decreased glomerular filtration rate -> Possible decrease in urine output -> 85%
CHAIN: Constriction of afferent arteriole -> Decreased renal blood flow -> Decreased glomerular filtration rate -> Unclear effect on urine output -> 70%
analysis: Constriction of the afferent arteriole reduces blood flow into the glomerulus, leading to a decrease in glomerular pressure and subsequently a reduction in the glomerular filtration rate (GFR). This results in decreased urinary output as less filtrate is produced.
